dimensions.assessment: Affects religious and charitable organizations seeking or maintaining federal tax-exempt status, as well as the Internal Revenue Service.
dimensions.evidence: a religious belief or practice concerning marriage, sexuality, or gender identity shall not be treated as being inconsistent with law or public policy

dimensions.assessment: Alters the legal standard by which the IRS evaluates tax-exempt charitable eligibility for organizations holding specific religious beliefs.
dimensions.evidence: an organization's religious beliefs or practices concerning marriage, sexuality, or gender identity may not be treated as inconsistent with public law or policy for purposes of determining whether the organization has a charitable purpose

dimensions.assessment: Implicates federal tax exemptions and tax-deductible contributions for qualifying religious organizations, though exact fiscal revenue effects are unstated in the source.
dimensions.evidence: exempt from federal income tax and receive tax-deductible contributions.

dimensions.assessment: Amends Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 by adding a new subsection regarding the determination of religious purpose.
dimensions.evidence: Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
dimensions.evidence: The amendment made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

missing_information: Estimated revenue loss or change to the federal budget resulting from the tax-exempt status rule change.
Number of organizations expected to be affected.
importance_detail.rationale: Amends the Internal Revenue Code to prevent religious beliefs concerning marriage, sexuality, or gender identity from being treated as inconsistent with public law or policy when determining tax-exempt charitable status.
